card.summary: Free plan: 8 Mbps speed limit, 4 tunnels, 1 free domain, unlimited traffic. [translated]

free_tier.stated: Free plan: 8 Mbps speed limit, 4 tunnels, 1 free domain, unlimited traffic. [translated]

egress.terms: The site says 'free and unlimited traffic, no need to worry about running out', while bandwidth can be limited for what the vendor calls excessive use.; ingress: udp

record.interface_detail: frpc client plus a documented REST API for nodes and tunnels.
record.tooling: frpc with a vendor-issued config; wg-quick on the local side
record.chaining: A UDP tunnel on an international node can carry a WG handshake at up to 32 Mbps, enough in principle for 1 TiB/month.
record.binding_note: With no byte quota the rate cap is what bites: 8 Mbps sustained is about 2.6 TB per month, so 1 TiB/month fits under it, but any burst above 8 Mbps is shaped, and bandwidth limiting is also possible.

identity_cost.detail: The mapping tutorial lists 'registered a ChmlFrp account and completed real-name verification' as a precondition, and says an unverified account shows 'you are not yet real-name verified' on the home page.

record.reliability_note: Node API exposes a per-node UDP flag, so a node can silently stop carrying UDP; the FAQ documents nodes going offline or being abandoned.
record.confidence_note: Unlimited traffic, the 8/32 Mbps split and the real-name precondition are all on vendor pages read. Only a probe could show the shaper's real behaviour.

evidence.proved: free plan is 8 Mbps, 4 tunnels, unlimited traffic
real-name verification is a stated precondition; port type includes UDP
each node reports whether UDP is allowed
bandwidth can be limited despite the unlimited-traffic claim
'If you are using a TCP or UDP tunnel ... the final address is your-domain:external-port', for example test.domain.cn:12345 [translated]

record.notes: Free frp provider offering unmetered transfer with a 32 Mbps international bandwidth limit. Registration requires national identity verification.

extras.wg_detail: The mapping guide lists TCP, UDP, HTTP and HTTPS as port types, and the public node API returns a per-node 'udp' boolean, so UDP carriage depends on the chosen node.
extras.volume_stated: The site says 'free and unlimited traffic, no need to worry about running out', while bandwidth can be limited for what the vendor calls excessive use.
